title: Ask the Board of Zoning Appeals for a variance, or appeal a zoning decision
question: I need relief from a setback or other zoning rule, or I disagree with the Zoning Administrator. What can I do?
office: Board of Zoning Appeals (Planning & Zoning Division is the City's liaison to the board)
summary: Staunton's Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA), five residents appointed by the Circuit Court, grants variances from lot and building rules such as setbacks and hears appeals of the Zoning Administrator's decisions. A variance cannot change a property's use. For a variance, talk with Planning & Zoning, then file the City's variance form, two copies of a plan and the $200 fee at Community Development in City Hall. To appeal, file the City's appeal form stating your grounds, with $200, within 30 days of the written decision (10 days for some violations). After published and mailed notice, the BZA holds a public hearing and must decide within 90 days. Its decision can be taken to Staunton Circuit Court within 30 days.

steps.step: Pick the right route: a variance, an appeal, or another process
steps.who: Property owner, tenant or other applicant; Planning & Zoning staff (Community Development) can advise
steps.how: Ask the BZA for a variance when a dimensional rule for a lot or building (lot area or width, front, side or rear setback, street frontage, or the size, height, bulk or location of a building) would unreasonably restrict use of the property; the City's variance form has rows for total area, lot width, front, minimum side, total side and rear yard setbacks, public street frontage and 'other'. A variance cannot allow a use the district does not permit or change the zoning; that needs a rezoning or special use permit, which are separate Planning & Zoning applications. Appeal to the BZA instead when you disagree with a written order, requirement, decision, determination or notice of violation of the Zoning Administrator, or want the BZA to interpret the zoning map or Code (the appeal form offers both). Entrance Corridor design review has its own route in the City Code: Planning Commission review, then an appeal to City Council within 30 days (City Code §§ 18.83.060(3), 18.83.070), on a separate City form (f4).
steps.quote: It shall not include a change in use, which change shall be accomplished by a rezoning or by a conditional zoning.

steps.step: For an appeal: have the Zoning Administrator's decision in writing, or ask for one
steps.who: The person who disagrees (owner, tenant, neighbor or other aggrieved person); the Zoning Administrator (Planning & Zoning Division)
steps.how: The BZA hears appeals from an administrative officer's order, requirement, decision or determination. A written notice of violation or written order must tell you that you may have a right to appeal within 30 days, give the appeal fee and say where to get more information. If you have no written decision, ask Planning & Zoning for one in writing. The City's fee list has a $75 Zoning Official Determination Letter, and its forms list has a Zoning Verification Letter request ($75; the form says up to two weeks). If you are not the owner or the owner's agent, the owner must be given written notice of your request within 10 days of its receipt, by the Zoning Administrator or, if directed, by you.
steps.deadline: The Zoning Administrator must respond within 90 days of a request for a decision or determination unless the requester has agreed to a longer period (Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4); City Code § 18.195.010(4))
steps.fee: $75.00 for a Zoning Official Determination Letter (City fee list); the verification letter form also shows $75.00
steps.quote: The zoning administrator shall respond within 90 days of a request for a decision or determination on zoning matters within the scope of his authority unless the requester has agreed to a longer period.

steps.step: For a variance: talk with Planning & Zoning staff before filing
steps.who: Applicant; Planning & Zoning staff, Community Development, City Hall 3rd floor
steps.how: Page 1 of the City's variance form is an acknowledgement that staff has discussed the standard for review with you, signed by you; if you are not the owner you agree to give the information to the owner. Ask staff which Code section and measurement apply, and whether another approval could give the relief, because a variance is not available when a special exception or an administrative modification could. Page 1 states the standard from a 2004 court case; the current standard is the one in Va. Code § 15.2-2309(2) and City Code § 18.200.010(2) (see caveats).
steps.quote: I acknowledge that the Planning & Inspections staff has discussed the "Standard for Review of Variance Applications" with me.

steps.step: For a variance: pay any delinquent real estate taxes on the property
steps.how: Before an application for a variance (or any other land-use application) is started, the applicant must show that any delinquent real estate taxes owed to the City and properly assessed against the property have been paid (City Code § 18.195.040). State law allows the requirement.
steps.quote: the authorizing body may require the applicant to produce satisfactory evidence that any delinquent real estate taxes, nuisance charges, stormwater management utility fees, and any other charges that constitute a lien on the subject property, that are owed to the locality and have been properly assessed against the subject property, have been paid

steps.step: For a variance: file the Application for Variance, plans and fee with Planning & Zoning
steps.who: Any property owner, tenant, government official, department, board or bureau; a representative may be listed on the form, but the owner signs
steps.how: Complete the City's Application for Variance: property address, parcel number, current zoning, water and sewer, what you want to build, and for each standard involved (total area, lot width, front yard setback, minimum and total side yard setback, rear yard setback, public street frontage, other) the Code section, what you have, what the Code requires and the variance requested. Answer the form's four questions (how the ordinance restricts use of the property; what about its size, shape or topography differs from other property in the area; the effect on other property; why you cannot comply another way). Attach two copies of a plan. The owner's signature lets the BZA and City staff enter the property. File with the fee at Community Development, City Hall 3rd floor, 116 W. Beverley St. (mail: P.O. Box 58). The pages read do not say whether the online permit portal takes variance applications.
steps.fee: $200.00 (Zoning Variance or Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals); not refunded once the case has been advertised
steps.quote: Two copies of a plan must be submitted with this application, showing size and location of the lot, dimensions and location of the proposed building or structure, and the dimensions and location of the existing structures on the lot.

steps.step: For an appeal: file the appeal with the Zoning Administrator and the BZA within 30 days
steps.who: Any person aggrieved, or any City officer, department, board or bureau affected by the decision
steps.how: File a notice of appeal stating your grounds with the Zoning Administrator and with the BZA; the City's form is 'Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals'. It asks for the date of the Zoning Administrator's decision, the property and its legal description, the Zoning Code provision, whether you want an interpretation of the zoning map or Code or an appeal of an administrative decision, a description of the problem, earlier appeals, special use permits or variances on the property, your interest in the property (owner, contract purchaser with the contract attached, owner's agent, other), the intended use, and supporting material such as a site plan or tax map. File it with the fee at Community Development. An appeal stays all proceedings in furtherance of the decision unless the Zoning Administrator certifies to the BZA that a stay would cause imminent peril to life or property; then only a restraining order from the BZA or a court of record, applied for on notice to the Zoning Administrator and for good cause shown, can stop them.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the decision appealed from; 10 days for notices of short-term, recurring violations (temporary or seasonal commercial uses, commercial trucks parked in residential districts, residential occupancy limits and similar) under City Code § 18.200.020(5). For a written notice of violation or written order of the Zoning Administrator, the period does not start until the notice's statement of appeal rights has been given and the order has been sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery to, or posted at, the owner's (or registered agent's) last known address or usual place of abode; that statement must also say that the decision becomes final and unappealable if not appealed within 30 days (Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A)).
steps.fee: $200.00 (Zoning Variance or Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals)
steps.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

steps.step: Staff sends the case to the BZA (and a variance to the Planning Commission) and shares its materials with you
steps.who: Zoning Administrator; secretary of the BZA; Planning Commission
steps.how: The application, or for an appeal all the papers making up the record of the decision, goes to the BZA's secretary, who puts the matter on the BZA docket. A copy of a variance application goes to the Planning Commission, which may send a recommendation or appear as a party at the hearing. Any staff report or other material given to a board member must be given to you free. You, the landowner or your agent or attorney may talk to a board member before the hearing, but not about the facts or law of the case.
steps.deadline: Materials given to board members: to the applicant or appellant as soon as practicable, and no more than three business days after
steps.quote: but in no event more than three business days of providing such materials to a member of the board

steps.step: The hearing is advertised and neighbors are notified
steps.who: Board of Zoning Appeals, with Planning & Zoning staff
steps.how: No variance may be considered, and no appeal decided, without notice and a public hearing under Va. Code § 15.2-2204: notice published twice in a newspaper with general circulation in the City, and notice to the owners, agents or occupants of abutting property and property across the street or road, which the BZA may send by first-class mail. For a variance, the City's form says the application fee cannot be refunded once the case has been advertised, whatever the board decides.
steps.deadline: First newspaper notice no more than 28 days, and the second no less than five days, before the hearing
steps.fee: No separate notice charge is on the City's fee list, so as far as the City's pages show it is covered by the $200.00 application fee; state law taxes the costs of notices required under the zoning chapter to the applicant (Va. Code § 15.2-2204(B)), so ask staff whether advertising or mailing costs are billed separately
steps.quote: with the first notice appearing no more than 28 days before and the second notice appearing no less than five days before the date of the meeting referenced in the notice

steps.step: Present the case at the BZA public hearing
steps.who: Board of Zoning Appeals (five Staunton residents appointed by the Staunton Circuit Court, City Code § 18.195.020); applicant or appellant; Zoning Administrator; the public
steps.how: The board must give the applicant or appellant and City staff equal time. On an appeal, the Zoning Administrator explains the decision first; it is presumed correct and you must rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence. On a variance, you must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that strict application of the ordinance would unreasonably restrict use of the property (or that the variance relieves a hardship from a physical condition, or is a reasonable modification for a person with a disability), and that: you acquired the property in good faith and did not create the hardship; nearby property will not suffer substantial detriment; the condition is not so general that the ordinance should be amended instead; no new use or zoning change results; and the relief is not available by special exception or administrative modification. The City Code adds that a variance must be the minimum adjustment necessary for reasonable use of the land, cannot vary a standard in another part of the City Code, and cannot let a principal or accessory building exceed the zoning code's maximum size standards (§ 18.200.010(2)(h) to (j)).
steps.quote: At a hearing on an appeal, the administrative officer shall explain the basis for his determination after which the appellant has the burden of proof to rebut such presumption of correctness by a preponderance of the evidence.

steps.how: The board may reverse, affirm or modify the decision appealed from (and may grant a variance on an appeal), or grant or deny the variance, and may attach conditions and require a bond or guarantee. Reversing the Zoning Administrator or granting a variance needs the concurring vote of a majority of the whole membership (3 of 5 members when the board has five). If an appeal vote ties, the person who appealed may ask to carry it over to the next scheduled meeting. Minutes are kept and are public records.
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the filing of the application or appeal
steps.quote: The concurring vote of a majority of the membership of the board shall be necessary to reverse any order, requirement, decision or determination of an administrative officer or to decide in favor of the applicant on any matter upon which it is required to pass under the ordinance or to effect any variance from the ordinance.

steps.step: After a variance is granted: meet its conditions and apply for permits
steps.who: Property owner; Planning & Zoning; Building Services
steps.how: Build only what the variance and its conditions allow, and apply for the zoning and building permits the work needs, online through the City's permit portal or on paper at Community Development. The property is then treated as conforming, but the structure may not be expanded into an area that would itself need a variance without a new variance.
steps.quote: the property upon which a property owner has been granted a variance shall be treated as conforming for all purposes under state law and local ordinance

steps.step: If you disagree with the BZA's decision: petition the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.who: Any person aggrieved by the decision, any aggrieved taxpayer, or a City officer, department, board or bureau; filed with the Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.how: File a petition with the Clerk specifying your grounds, styled "[Petitioner v. Respondent] In Re: [date] Decision of the Board of Zoning Appeals of [locality name]". The governing body (City Council), the applicant and the landowner of record (if not the applicant) are necessary parties, listed as petitioner or respondent. Serve them and the BZA's secretary (or chair) within 30 days after filing; later service counts as timely only if the court finds you used due diligence, and failure to file and serve on time leads to dismissal. Filing does not stay the decision unless the court grants a temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction. The court presumes a variance decision correct and the BZA's factual findings on an appeal correct, unless you prove error by a preponderance of the evidence; it decides questions of law afresh.
steps.deadline: Petition within 30 days after the BZA's final decision (mandatory and jurisdictional); service within 30 days after the petition is filed
steps.fee: Circuit court filing costs were not confirmed; ask the Clerk's Office
steps.quote: Such 30-day filing requirement shall be mandatory and jurisdictional.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The newest copies are from 2026-05-07 to 2026-06-10, so changes since then are not reflected. The city's Web Disclaimer & Privacy Policy sets no limit on quoting site content. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

The Board of Zoning Appeals' own page is on stauntonva.granicus.com (embedded on the City's Boards & Commissions page), which refuses automated readers, so its membership, meeting schedule, rules of procedure, filing deadlines and any notes posted there are not described here.

Local law: the Staunton City Code is published on General Code's eCode360, whose terms limit use to personal purposes and forbid reproducing content for public purposes. Chapters 18.83, 18.195, 18.200 and 18.220 were read to find section numbers and to check that the steps match, but no eCode360 text is quoted; the local legal_basis entries therefore carry no quote. eCode360 showed three new laws not yet codified, including Ord. 2026-26 (2026-09-10) amending the district regulations; none was read, and none appeared to affect the BZA chapters.

City Code § 18.200.030 (court review, last amended by Ord. 2016-15) still describes a writ of certiorari and a shorter petition style. Va. Code § 15.2-2314, rewritten since (2017, 2020 and 2026 amendments in the index), sets the current petition style, necessary parties, 30-day service and standards of review; step s12 follows state law.

The City's variance form is old: its PDF metadata dates are 2016-11-02 and 2018-02-12, it carries the former 'Department of Planning & Inspections' name, and page 1 states the 'all reasonable beneficial uses' standard of Cochran v. Fairfax County BZA (2004). The General Assembly replaced that standard in 2015 (Va. Code § 15.2-2309, 2015 c. 597), and the City followed in Ord. 2016-15 (City Code § 18.200.010). The form also says a Zoning Code section is attached, but the PDF has none. Ask staff whether a newer form exists. Both BZA forms are scans with a machine (OCR) text layer; quotes were copied from that text layer and could not be checked against the page images, and the layer has OCR slips elsewhere ('ofthe', 'lfl').

Forms: the appeal form has a 'Fee Paid' line but does not state the fee or the deadline. None of the four PDFs has fillable fields (the variance PDF has an empty AcroForm with no widgets), so fillable is false. The Entrance Corridor form (f4) is listed with the BZA forms on the City's Permits page, but City Code §§ 18.83.060(3) and 18.83.070 send Entrance Corridor design disputes to the Planning Commission, with an appeal to City Council within 30 days and then to the circuit court within 30 days; that route is not modeled here.

Online filing: since May 5, 2026 the City takes permit applications through its online portal (Tyler EnerGov), and paper filing at Community Development is still available. The Planning & Zoning page lists online submittal only for zoning permits (home occupation, apiary, chickens, real estate temporary office, signs); whether variance or appeal applications can be filed online was not confirmed, and the portal was not entered (account required).

No BZA filing deadline, submittal calendar or meeting schedule was found. The City's board agendas page lists the Board of Zoning Appeals; the only BZA listing found in the archive (2022-03-07 capture) shows one meeting at 4:00 PM on 03/08/2022. The Planning & Zoning page's 'Planning & Zoning Applications' link points to a City admin address that is not public.

Asking for a determination: the fee list has a 'Zoning Official Determination Letter' ($75.00) and the forms list has an 'Application for a Zoning Verification Letter' ($75.00, up to two weeks). The sources do not say whether they are the same service or whether a verification letter is an appealable determination; ask for a written determination that states the appeal right.

Alternatives to a variance: Va. Code § 15.2-2309(2)(v) bars a variance when a special exception or an administrative modification (§ 15.2-2286(A)(4)) could give the relief. Whether Staunton's ordinance authorizes the Zoning Administrator to grant modifications was not confirmed (the chapters cited here do not mention one). Staunton's 'uses permitted on review' (Chapter 18.210) are not covered here. The 'Modification Application' on the City's Permits page is a Building Services form with a Building Official's signature line (archive copy 2026-04-13), so it appears to be a building code modification, not the Zoning Administrator's modification under § 15.2-2286(A)(4).

Fees: the fee page row is two table cells ('Zoning Variance or Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals' and '$200.00'); the quote joins them with a space. City Code § 18.220.020 lists the same $200.00 and $75.00 amounts and exempts projects by and on property owned and operated by the City or the School Board; that exemption has no quotable source. The sources do not say whether $200.00 stays within the state cap on appeal fees (§ 15.2-2311(A)) or how fees are paid. The fee list also has a 'Variance to Subdivision Ordinance' ($200.00); that is a subdivision matter, not a BZA zoning variance, and is not modelled here.

Short appeal period: City Code § 18.200.020(5) sets 10 days for notices of short-term, recurring violations (temporary or seasonal commercial uses, commercial trucks in residential districts, residential occupancy limits and similar). It does not list the storage or disposal of nonagricultural excavation material, waste and debris that state law also allows; for those the 30-day period appears to apply.

Missed deadlines: no consequence was found if the Zoning Administrator misses the 90-day response duty or the BZA misses its 90-day decision deadline (Va. Code §§ 15.2-2286(A)(4), 15.2-2312). The sources give no deemed approval, and remedies such as mandamus are not covered here. The no_answer rung is a suggested follow-up, not a legal remedy.
Re-filing: Va. Code § 15.2-2310 lets a locality bar substantially the same application for up to one year; no such bar was found in the chapters read.

Board size: City Code § 18.195.020 sets five members appointed by the circuit court, and state law allows five or seven. The '3 of 5' figure in step s10 is derived from that and the majority-of-the-membership rule in § 15.2-2312; with alternates or vacancies, ask staff how the count applies. No alternates for Staunton were found.

Court steps give the statutory deadlines only. Circuit court filing costs for a § 15.2-2314 petition, the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia, and the Court of Appeals' own rules were not read; the Court of Appeals rung assumes the petition is a civil matter under § 17.1-405(A)(3). The Staunton Circuit Court page (vacourts.gov, read 2026-10-11) gives 113 East Beverley Street, 2nd Floor, for the court, with the Clerk's Office on the third floor.

Other approvals: work in a historic district may also need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Commission, and floodplain rules (City Code Chapter 18.170) may apply; neither is covered here.

Versions: Open US Law's copy marks Va. Code §§ 15.2-2201 and 15.2-2286 'effective until January 1, 2027' and holds no successor text. Re-check the variance definition, the 90-day response duty and the short appeal periods on or after January 1, 2027. State quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the cited section; some keep that copy's space before punctuation after a cross-reference ('§ 15.2-2314 , and'). The law.lis.virginia.gov URLs are for reference.

Privacy: the Planning & Zoning and Community Development pages name staff, including the Zoning Administrator, and link personal staff mailboxes; the court page names the clerk and judges. None is recorded. Only office lines, office addresses and office pages are given; no role mailbox for Planning & Zoning was found.

corrections: Quotes: all 74 draft quotes confirmed. The 68 state-law quotes are whitespace-normalised substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (rows 2586, 2589, 2711, 2764-2769, 2771, 30346, 4663) and sit under the cited subsection or subdivision. The 6 local quotes (5 distinct; the $200.00 fee row appears twice) were re-read: the two fee rows on the Internet Archive copy of the Planning & Zoning Fees page (2026-05-10; each is two table cells joined by a space, as the caveat says) and three sentences in the text layer of the variance form (archive copy 2026-04-13).

6 quotes added and confirmed the same way, all state law: Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A) (final and unappealable if not appealed within 30 days), § 15.2-2311(B) (restraining order when a stay is refused), § 15.2-2204(B) (notice costs taxed to the applicant; in legal_basis and fees), § 15.2-2314(A) (dismissal for failure to file and serve on time), and § 15.2-2201 for a new referral rung. 80 quotes now, all confirmed.

s6 and escalation rung 1: the draft said the appeal period does not start until the notice is given and the order is mailed or posted, for every decision. Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A) ties that rule to a written notice of violation or written order with the appeal statement, sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery or posted. Both now say so, and s6 adds that the statement must say the decision becomes final and unappealable if not appealed within 30 days.

s6: 'stays enforcement' now follows § 15.2-2311(B): the appeal stays all proceedings in furtherance of the decision unless the Zoning Administrator certifies imminent peril, and then only a restraining order from the BZA or a court of record can stop them.

s8: the draft applied the no-refund rule to every case. It comes from the variance form only, so it is now stated for variances. The fee note now adds that § 15.2-2204(B) taxes notice costs to the applicant, with a matching fees entry.

s1: the draft called the listed standards (including height, bulk and location) 'the rows on the City's variance form'; the form's rows are total area, lot width, front, minimum side, total side and rear yard setbacks, public street frontage and other, and the sentence now says so. The Entrance Corridor sentence no longer says such disputes cannot go to the BZA (the City Code gives them a Planning Commission and City Council route; it does not say the BZA lacks jurisdiction).

s9: added the other local limits in City Code § 18.200.010(2): no variance of a standard in another part of the City Code, and none letting a principal or accessory building exceed the zoning code's maximum size standards (re-read on eCode360; not quoted).

s12: necessary parties now include the landowner of record only if different from the applicant, as § 15.2-2314(A) says; added the due-diligence rule for late service and dismissal for failure to file and serve on time.
s7: the materials deadline now includes 'as soon as practicable' before the three-business-day limit (§ 15.2-2308.1(B)).

Escalation: the no_answer rung was typed 'internal appeal', but no appeal lies to the head of Community Development; it is now 'oversight' (the caveat already calls it a suggested follow-up, not a legal remedy). Added a 'prerequisite' referral rung for a use or zoning change, which a variance cannot give (§§ 15.2-2201, 15.2-2309(2)(iv); City Code § 18.200.010(2)(e), (g)); the $250.00 rezoning or special use permit fee is confirmed on the fee page.
office: 'staffed by Planning & Zoning' now reads that the Planning & Zoning Division is the City's liaison to the board, as the Planning & Zoning page says.
